findings.claim: “between the respectable homes of Camberwell and the opium den in Upper Swandam Lane”
findings.truth: There is no opium den in The Sign of Four. Upper Swandam Lane is the setting of a different Holmes story, 'The Man with the Twisted Lip' (1891). The only mention of opium in this novel is Small's aside about rebels 'drunk with opium and with bang' (ch. 12).
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #2097: grep 'Swandam' returns nothing; grep 'opium' returns one hit, line 3871.

findings.claim: Watson describes a “dense drizzly fog” “as they travel to Pondicherry Lodge”
findings.truth: The fog passage is Chapter 3, on the cab ride to the Lyceum Theatre and then to Thaddeus Sholto's house. They do not reach Pondicherry Lodge until Chapter 5.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg line 687 (Chapter III, lines 596–781); the Lyceum rendezvous follows at line 3299 of that chapter.

findings.claim: “The 1880s also saw the creation of the Metropolitan Police’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID).”
findings.truth: The CID was founded in 1878. The lesson's own flashcard says 1878, and Lesson 3 says 1878, so the unit contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: L1 flashcard 11; L3 content_html n16.

findings.claim: “Understanding this context is essential For the exam .”
findings.truth: Stray capital letter and a space before the full stop.
findings.evidence: raw/L01.txt n3.

findings.claim: “Jonathan Small lost his leg serving in the Indian army” (repeated in practice question 4's mark scheme)
findings.truth: Small took the Queen's shilling and joined the 3rd Buffs, a British regiment sent to India. He lost the leg to a crocodile while swimming in the Ganges, not in action and not in the Indian army.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 3738–3745: 'joining the 3rd Buffs, which was just starting for India' / 'A crocodile took me, just as I was half-way'.

findings.claim: “Read the passage in Chapter 2 where Watson describes the journey through London to Thaddeus Sholto’s home”
findings.truth: That passage is Chapter 3.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg line 687, inside Chapter III (596–781).

findings.claim: Every lesson's question 5 ends “[34 marks including 4 marks for SPaG]” and its mark scheme runs “Top band (25–30 marks + 4 spelling/grammar)” down to “(1–2 marks + 1 spelling/grammar)”.
findings.truth: AQA 8702 Paper 1 Section B (the 19th-century novel) is a single 30-mark question: AO1 12, AO2 12, AO3 6. No SPaG marks are awarded on it. The 4 SPaG marks sit on the Section A Shakespeare question, which is why Paper 1 totals 64. Lesson 7's own knowledge check already gives the right answer, 30 marks.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md §2 (Paper 1, 64 marks) and §4.2/4.3; L7 knowledge_checks[1].

findings.claim: Every lesson's question 4 is labelled “30 marks — Essay” but its mark scheme runs “Top band (11-12)” down to “Lower band (1-2)”, and uses the label “Top band” twice.
findings.truth: The stated marks and the mark scheme contradict each other. Rebuilt as the AQA 30-mark level ladder (Level 6 = 26–30 down to Level 1 = 1–5) with the descriptors kept.
findings.evidence: raw/L01-L07.txt practice_questions[3].marks.

findings.claim: Headings “Chapter 3: Thaddeus Sholto” and “Chapter 4: The Horror at Pondicherry Lodge”, plus the crescendo paragraph and four practice-question stems.
findings.truth: Chapter 3 is 'In Quest of a Solution' (the foggy cab ride). Thaddeus Sholto is Chapter 4, 'The Story of the Bald-Headed Man'. Pondicherry Lodge and Bartholomew's body are Chapter 5, 'The Tragedy of Pondicherry Lodge'. Every chapter number from 3 onwards was one too low.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg contents, lines 40–51; chapter starts at lines 596, 782, 1148; body found at line 1344.

findings.claim: “Creosote on the rope used to enter through the roof” — repeated in L2 key fact and flashcard, L3 content, glossary and flashcard, and L6 content, key fact and flashcard.
findings.truth: The creosote is not on the rope. A carboy of creosote in Bartholomew's laboratory has cracked and leaked over the floor; Tonga treads in it. That footprint in the spilled creosote is what gives Toby a scent to follow.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 1580–1583: 'Number One has had the misfortune to tread in the creosote... The carboy has been cracked... and the stuff has leaked out.'

findings.claim: “Holmes warns: ‘It is a capital mistake to theorise before you have all the evidence. It biases the judgment.’” (also L3 flashcard 12)
findings.truth: That line is from A Study in Scarlet, not The Sign of Four. Replaced with Holmes in Chapter 1 of this novel: 'I never guess. It is a shocking habit — destructive to the logical faculty.'
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #2097: grep 'capital mistake' and 'biases the judg' return nothing; line 325 gives the replacement.

findings.claim: “Holmes responds with characteristic good humour: ‘I have been at some small expense over this matter, which I shall expect the county to refund.’”
findings.truth: Invented. Holmes says no such thing in this novel.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #2097: 'county' appears nowhere; 'expense' and 'refund' appear only in the Project Gutenberg licence text.

findings.claim: “Holmes deduces that the smaller intruder is from ‘one of the Indian islands’”
findings.truth: That phrase is not in the novel. Holmes reasons from the naked footprint and the blowpipe darts, then reads a gazetteer entry on the Andaman Islands in Chapter 8 to name the place.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 2596–2632; grep 'Indian island' returns nothing.

findings.claim: Headings “Chapter 5: Holmes at the Crime Scene”, “Chapter 6: Toby the Dog”, “Chapter 7: The Baker Street Irregulars”, “Chapter 8: Athelney Jones”, plus “Throughout Chapters 5–7” and three practice stems.
findings.truth: The crime-scene demonstration, the creosote and Athelney Jones are Chapter 6. Toby and the barrel are Chapter 7. The Irregulars are Chapter 8. Jones runs from Chapter 6 to the end, so his section carries no single chapter number.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg chapter starts: VI at 1438, VII at 1799, VIII at 2255; creosote at 1582, Toby at 1907, Wiggins at 2558.

findings.claim: “(Note: this famous line is from Chapter 6, not Chapter 5)”
findings.truth: An editorial note left inside student-facing content, contradicting the heading above it. Removed as part of the F14/F10 edit.
findings.evidence: raw/L03.txt n2.

findings.claim: “‘I would rather that our old cronies at Doolan had it than that a soul of us should benefit from it,’ he says.”
findings.truth: Invented, including the place name. Small's actual line is: 'It is my treasure; and if I can't have the loot I'll take darned good care that no one else does.'
findings.evidence: Gutenberg: grep 'cronies' and 'Doolan' return nothing; lines 3668–3671 give the real line.

findings.claim: “We were fairly flying through the water, the barges and the riverside buildings racing past us.” — quoted in the content and printed as the extract for practice question 1, whose mark scheme then analyses ‘fairly flying’ and ‘racing past us’.
findings.truth: Doyle wrote 'We were fairly after her now' and 'We flashed past barges, steamers, merchant-vessels, in and out, behind this one and round the other', with the engines 'like a great metallic heart'. The quoted sentence does not exist.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 3286–3295.

findings.claim: “A Sikh servant named Abdullah Khan… They murdered the merchant and swore a pact”
findings.truth: Abdullah Khan and Mahomet Singh are Sikh soldiers ('tall, fierce-looking chaps… both old fighting-men') on guard with Small at the Agra fort gate, not servants. Small also swore the oath before the killing, not after it.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 3862–3864 and 3927–3936.

findings.claim: “Chapter 9: The Thames Chase”, “Chapter 10: Jonathan Small’s Confession”, “Chapters 11 and 12 are Jonathan Small’s extended confession”, “Chapter 12: The Ending”.
findings.truth: Chapter 9 is 'A Break in the Chain'; the chase is Chapter 10, 'The End of the Islander'. Chapter 11 is Watson taking the empty box to Mary and proposing. The confession is Chapter 12 alone. The collapsible heading and the paragraph inside it also contradicted each other.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg chapter starts: IX 2648, X 3074, XI 3409, XII 3640; chase at 3286–3395; proposal at 3615–3638; Small begins his story at 3729.

findings.claim: “Tonga fires a poison dart… Holmes and Watson return fire”
findings.truth: The pistols go off as Tonga raises the blowpipe to his lips; the dart 'must have whizzed between us at the instant that we fired'. The lesson reverses the order, which matters because the lesson itself discusses how readily Tonga is shot.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 3364–3402.

findings.claim: “(as established in A Study in Scarlet; The Sign of Four only mentions a old wound without naming the Battle of Maiwand specifically)”
findings.truth: The Jezail bullet is named in The Sign of Four itself, in Chapter 1: 'I had a Jezail bullet through it some time before.' The bracket also carried a grammar slip, 'a old wound'.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg line 160.

findings.claim: “a firm set of her lips”, given as a quotation for Mary Morstan — in the content, in practice question 2's mark scheme, and in flashcard 10.
findings.truth: Not in the novel. Doyle's words for Mary's composure are 'her sensitive face was composed, but pale' and 'her self-control was perfect' (Chapter 3). 'Sweet and amiable' is correct (Chapter 2).
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 389–391 and 645–649; grep 'set of her lips' returns nothing.

findings.claim: “Chapters 11–12” given as the span of Small's confession — in L5 content, L6 content, L6 practice question 6, L6 knowledge check 2 and L6 flashcard 7.
findings.truth: The embedded confession is Chapter 12 only. Chapter 11, 'The Great Agra Treasure', is Watson's narration of the empty box and the proposal.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 3409 and 3640; Small begins to speak at line 3722.

findings.claim: “Watson narrates events in the present tense as they unfold in London.”
findings.truth: Watson narrates in the past tense throughout. Naming the wrong tense would cost a student credibility on an AO2 point about narrative method.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg, whole text: 'I stooped to the hole, and recoiled in horror' (line 1337), etc.

findings.claim: “Watson describes ‘the dull blur of the lights’ along the dockside, timber yards, and the ‘dense swarm’ of boats.”
findings.truth: 'Dense swarm' is not in the novel at all. 'The dull blur' describes the Aurora ahead of them on the water, not dockside lights.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg line 3317: 'The dull blur in front of us resolved itself now clearly enough into the dainty Aurora'; grep 'dense swarm' returns nothing.

findings.claim: “the foggy journey in Chapter 2” and “the journey through London in Chapter 2”
findings.truth: Chapter 3.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg line 687, inside Chapter III.

findings.claim: The “Key Quotations to Learn” list ends with “It is a capital mistake to theorise before you have all the evidence” (also flashcard 11).
findings.truth: A memorisation list for this novel contained a line from a different novel, A Study in Scarlet. A student quoting it in the exam would be quoting a text they were not asked about. Replaced with Holmes in Chapter 1 of The Sign of Four: 'Detection is, or ought to be, an exact science.'
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #2097: grep 'capital mistake' returns nothing; line 139–140 gives the replacement.

findings.claim: “Watson is relieved: ‘the treasure is lost and the case is closed’”
findings.truth: An invented composite. 'The treasure is lost' is Mary Morstan's line, not Watson's, and 'the case is closed' is nowhere in the novel. Watson's own words are 'the golden barrier was gone from between us'.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 3615 and 3620–3622; grep 'case is closed' returns nothing.

findings.claim: Lesson titles “Chapters 1-4: The Mystery Begins” and “Chapters 5-8: The Chase”.
findings.truth: Once the chapter numbers inside the lessons are corrected (F9, F14), L2 covers Chapters 1–5 and L3 covers Chapters 6–8. Title is not one of the fields this pass may edit. Options: (a) retitle L2 to 'Chapters 1–5: The Mystery Begins' and L3 to 'Chapters 6–8: The Chase', which I recommend and which leaves L4 'Chapters 9-12' correct; or (b) leave the titles and accept a one-chapter overlap between the stated range and the content.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg contents lines 40–51.

findings.claim: Each lesson carries two “4 marks — Quote Analysis” and two “8 marks — Extract Analysis” items, and several of the 8-mark stems say “Write about the extract and the novel as a whole” without printing an extract.
findings.truth: AQA Section B is one 30-mark extract question, so no 4-mark or 8-mark question exists on this paper. These look like deliberate platform-wide scaffolding rather than a Sign of Four error, so I have not touched them. If the programme wants them aligned, the fix is either to print an extract or to drop the 'write about the extract' clause. This is a fleet-level decision, not a unit one.
findings.evidence: specs/aqa/english-literature-8702-8702.md §2.

findings.claim: “Check your exam board’s specimen paper for the exact mark weightings that apply to you.”
findings.truth: Not false, but oddly board-neutral in an AQA-specific unit whose own knowledge check already states 30 marks. Left alone because it makes no wrong claim.
findings.evidence: raw/L07.txt n17.

findings.claim: “A poison dart is embedded in his scalp”
findings.truth: Doyle writes 'a long, dark thorn stuck in the skin just above the ear', and later has Holmes call the same things 'little darts' shot from a blow-pipe. Both words are defensible and 'just above the ear' is still scalp, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 1390–1391 and 2597.

summary: All seven lessons carry findings. 28 are FIX (9 HIGH, 16 MEDIUM, 3 LOW), plus 2 ADJUDICATE and 2 NOTE. The worst are five invented or misattributed quotations (the 'capital mistake' line from A Study in Scarlet in a memorisation list, the 'county to refund' line, the 'cronies at Doolan' line, the Thames-chase line printed as an extract, and 'a firm set of her lips'), the opium den imported from 'The Man with the Twisted Lip', the creosote wrongly placed on the rope in three lessons, and a false claim in every lesson that this 30-mark Section B question is worth 34 marks including 4 for SPaG. Chapter numbers run one too low from Chapter 3 onwards through Lessons 2, 3 and 4. 82 edits written.
